_about: Example machine overlay. Copy it to settings.machine.json in the harness home (untracked, gitignored), keep only the keys you need and replace every demo value with your own. scripts/bootstrap writes a minimal overlay (modules + env.CLAUDE_HOME) only when none exists and never edits an existing one; on a home upgraded from code before the settings filter, the landing (scripts/install/land, run by hooks/auto-commit.sh) migrates one once instead; agents never write it. The settings filter renders clean form + enabled modules + overlay into the working settings.json (git smudge, or scripts/install/render-settings render) and removes everything a module, the overlay or the record of what smudge and render applied (<git dir>/claude-settings.applied, never tracked) added, plus the CLI-owned keys, when git stores settings.json (git clean), so nothing from this file reaches a commit, even after a value is removed from it before the next render. render-settings check --staged (pre-commit hook and CI) refuses every commit while this file is in the index; git rm --cached -- settings.machine.json untracks it.
_format: Top-level keys whose names start with "_" (like this one) are documentation and are never rendered.
"modules" is meta and never rendered: module name -> true or false. An unknown module name is an error.
"env": every key is set in the rendered env (replacing a clean-form value of the same name, otherwise appended). Put no documentation inside env: every env key is rendered.
"permissions".allow / .deny / .ask: every entry is appended unless already present. The overlay cannot remove or weaken a clean-form entry.
"hooks".<event>: every group is appended to that event; a group whose "hooks" list equals an existing group's "hooks" list instead adds its "|"-separated matcher alternatives to that group.
Any other top-level key (the CLI-owned keys below, or e.g. cleanupPeriodDays) replaces the clean-form value.
Layer order: the enabled modules in sorted name order, then this overlay.

_modules.paseo: Optional paseo integration, default false. When true the module adds the allow entries mcp__paseo__* and Bash(node scripts/paseo-usage-read.mjs:*), the UserPromptSubmit hook hooks/userprompt-usage-snapshot.py, and the mcp__paseo__browser_run_code matcher alternative on the PreToolUse and PostToolUse runcode-watchdog groups. Its env settings are PASEO_DAEMON_ACCOUNTS and PASEO_DAEMON_MODEL.

_env.CLAUDE_HOME: Absolute path of the harness home (this checkout). Written by scripts/bootstrap. Every hook command resolves "${CLAUDE_HOME:-$HOME/.claude}", so without it hooks fall back to $HOME/.claude.
_env.TMPDIR: Scratch directory for sessions and tools. The clean form pins /var/tmp/claude-scratch; override TMPDIR and CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR together. scripts/bootstrap creates the directory (mode 1777) if it is absent.
_env.CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR: Claude Code's own scratch directory; keep it equal to TMPDIR.
_env.GIT_AUTO_PUSH: Optional opt-in, not set in this example. The clean form sets "0" (no automatic push); add "GIT_AUTO_PUSH": "1" to env only if this machine wants automatic remote backup.
_env.CLAUDE_DEV_CONTAINERS: Whitespace-separated exact names of dev containers the agent may docker stop/restart/rm/kill. Default empty: no container is whitelisted.
_env.CLAUDE_DAEMON_RESTART_GRANT_HELPER: Path of the operator's helper that grants a one-time daemon restart; it is only named in the daemon-restart guidance text. Default empty.
_env.CLAUDE_PROTECTED_DAEMON_PREFIX: Unit-name prefix of a local daemon the agent must never restart (systemctl or wrapper). Default empty: the daemon-restart prohibition layers are inert.
_env.CLAUDE_PROTECTED_DAEMON_TARGETS: "|"-separated per-instance suffixes of the protected daemon (units <prefix>-<target>). Default empty.
_env.CLAUDE_HARD_BANNED_SCRIPTS: Scripts the agent may never run, as EREs separated by "|" (empty entries are skipped). A non-empty value replaces the default, and each of its EREs is matched anywhere in the command, so reading or naming a matching file is blocked too. Default (unset or empty): the names session-recovery and restart-all-sessions, matched only as the command word (NAME or NAME.sh, any directory path, also after an assignment, a < redirect or a listed wrapper or shell such as sudo, timeout 30 or bash -x), so reading, listing, editing or naming the file passes unless the name stands right after a command separator such as ; | or (, even inside quotes; list them in a set value to keep them, then matched anywhere. The demo value below names stand-ins only, so setting it drops the default names.
_env.CLAUDE_PROTECTED_PROCESS_FAMILY: Process family word: docker stop/restart/rm/kill on a container matching it is blocked, and killall/pkill of it is blocked alongside claude and docker. Default empty: the docker rule is inert and the kill rule covers claude and docker only.
_env.CLAUDE_RESTART_ACCOUNTS_ROOT: Root of sibling Claude Code accounts that /restart also scans (<root>/<name>/claude/projects/<slug>/). Unset or empty: only ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/projects is scanned.
_env.WORKFLOW_PRUNE_ACCOUNTS_DIR: Accounts root scanned by scripts/prune-orphaned-workflow-bookmarks.sh. Default empty: no account scan.
_env.WORKFLOW_PRUNE_PROJECT_DIRNAME: Claude Code project directory name of the harness home. Default derived from the realpath of the resolved harness home (every character other than an ASCII letter or digit becomes "-"), so set it only when that derivation does not fit.
_env.CLAUDE_CHECKPOINT_EXTRA_TRAILER: One extra trailer line appended after the Claude Co-Authored-By trailer on checkpoint commits. Default empty: no extra trailer.
_env.GRAPHIFY_BIN: Path of the graphify CLI (PyPI graphifyy), the optional code-graph tool. scripts/graphify_lib.py runs it for scripts/graphify-query.py, graphify-enrich.py and graphify-maintain.py; hooks/prompt-workflow.py writes the /dev graphify sentinel only when this is set or a graphify binary is found. Default unset: graphify on PATH (the prompt hook also accepts <harness home>/venv/bin/graphify). A set path that does not exist makes the scripts treat graphify as absent, with no PATH fallback.
_env.PASEO_DAEMON_ACCOUNTS: paseo module: comma-separated account names, the --accounts default of scripts/paseo-daemon-ledger.py; its init refuses when no account is given.
_env.PASEO_DAEMON_MODEL: paseo module: model used by scripts/paseo-daemon-timers.py, in the form <model-id>@<account>. Default: the built-in model id without an account suffix.

_permissions: Personal permission entries: tool paths outside the harness, machine-only MCP servers, extra denies. They are appended to the clean form's lists. Bash rules match the literal command text (no ~ or variable expansion), so write each path exactly as it is typed.

_hooks.about: Optional machine-only hook groups, same shape as the hooks key of settings.json. Use the harness-home channel in the command and keep the script under the harness home: the doctor requires every hook command to resolve to a file there. To use one, copy it into a top-level "hooks" key; this documentation key is never rendered.

_cli_owned: model, theme, tui, alwaysThinkingEnabled, effortLevel and autoCompactEnabled are written by Claude Code itself (/model, /config, /effort). The clean form carries none of them. Values set here are this machine's defaults in the rendered settings.json; once Claude Code has written a value into the working file, render keeps that value. The clean filter strips these keys (and modelSettings, fastMode, advisorModel) so they never reach a commit.

_private_literals.path: <harness home>/private-literals.txt (untracked, gitignored). Fixed: no setting or environment variable changes it, and it is not part of this overlay.
_private_literals.about: Personal literals that must never appear in a tracked file: account names, e-mail addresses, private host, product, unit or container names, personal home paths. scripts/bootstrap creates the file empty (0 bytes, mode 0600) if absent and the human fills it; on a home upgraded from code before the settings filter, the landing (scripts/install/land) seeds it once, while it is absent or empty, from values the machine already holds and never rewrites a list that has lines. The pre-commit hook runs scripts/check-public-core.sh --private-literals over what the staged change adds (its added lines, and the paths of files it adds or changes) and refuses the commit when any literal occurs, reporting file:line and the literal's line number in the list, never the literal itself. Checkpoint snapshots run the same rule over what their temporary index adds over HEAD, and a plain scripts/check-public-core.sh run over every file in the index (the content as staged, not the working tree). render-settings check --staged refuses every commit while this list is in the index.
_private_literals.format: One literal per line. Blank lines and lines whose first non-blank character is # are ignored. Matching is case-sensitive and fixed-string (no patterns, no wildcards).
